text_blocks.snippet: Herpes zoster, also known as shingles, is treated with antiviral medications, pain management, and in some cases, corticosteroids. Antiviral drugs like acyclovir, valacyclovir, and famciclovir help shorten the duration and severity of the illness, especially when started early. Pain relief, which can include over-the-counter or prescription pain relievers, is crucial for comfort and can involve narcotic or non-narcotic analgesics, and even neuroactive agents or anticonvulsants in some cases. Corticosteroids may be used to reduce inflammation and pain, particularly in older patients, but their effectiveness in preventing postherpetic neuralgia is debated.
